clean: Dear Professor Lindpist, I'm writing on behalf of the microscopy group to ask about the booking schedule for the electron microscope next semester. Right now we have three slots on Tuesdays and two on Thursdays, but our new postdocs need at least 6 hours a week to finish the imaging for the grant report. Could we move one of the Thursday slots to Wednesday afternoon, because the technician is only in until noon? I've also attached the list of samples, which is about 40 in total. Please let me know if that works or if you'd rather talk it through in person. Kind regards, Shira

Hi Marta, thanks for sending over the incident notes from Saturday night. I went through them this morning and I've got a couple of thoughts. First off, the guest in room 412 was not offered the late checkout like the log says, he was just told it might be possible, which is not the same thing. Second, the night auditor should have called me before coming the breakfast, that's over the threshold we agreed on, which was $50. I don't want to make it a big deal though, I think it's mostly a training gap. Can we sit down Friday at 10 and go through the escalation sheet together? I'll bring coffee. Talk soon, Aika

Good afternoon Mr. Reeds

I am writing to confirm that our crew will be on site at the pumping station on the 14th of October to replace the isolation valve. As discussed, the work will require a planned shutdown of the east zone supply from 8 in the morning until roughly 4 in the afternoon. We will notify the roughly 1,200 affected households by letter and by text message at least 72 hours in advance.

If the weather turns, we will reschedule for the following week and let you know by the previous evening. Please call me directly on 555-0142 if anything changes on your side. Sincerely
Damian O'Conco

Okay, quick recap of the camping trip planning because I know everybody's been asking. We're leaving Friday at around 3, which means if you work late you should meet us at the campsite instead of the house. It's the lakeside one, site number 22, and the gate closes at 9, so please don't show up at 10 like last year. Pedro is bringing the big tent and the stove, Celen has the cooler, and I'm handling the firewood and the s'mores stuff. We still need someone to bring a second lantern and probably more water, at least 10 liters. Oh, and the forecast says rain on Sunday morning, so pack a tarp. That's about it, shout if I forgot anything.

Hi Layla, I hope the book club meeting went well last night, sorry I couldn't make it. I did finish the novel on the train though and I have a lot of feelings about the ending. I thought the first two thirds were brilliant, the way the author lets the sister's letters carry the story, but then the last 40 pages felt rushed, like she ran out of room. I'd love to hear what everyone else thought. Also, could you add me to the thread for next month? I heard we're doing something by a translator I've never read, and I'm really excited about that, honestly. One more thing, I can host in November if nobody else wants to, I just need a heads up of about two weeks. Thanks so much, Snora

Hello everyone, a few updates from the front desk before the weekend rush. One, we've switched to the new key card system, so if your card stops working please come see us and don't try to reset it yourself. Two, breakfast now ends at 10:30 on weekdays and 11 on weekends, which I know some of you were asking about. Three, the lift on the north side is out of order until at least Tuesday, so guests with luggage should be directed to the main lift. Also, just a reminder that we're fully booked on Saturday, so no walk-ins, please, I can't stress that enough. Thank you all for your hard work, it really does not go unnoticed. Cheers, She run

Following up on our chat in the corridor. What I was trying to say is that the freelance budget for the features desk is basically gone for this quarter, so any new commissions will have to wait until January. I know that's frustrating, especially since you already have the profile of the ferry captain half written. What I can do is pay you for the work so far, say £400, and hold the piece for the new year. I'd also like to see the photo permissions sorted out before then, because legal flagged that last time. Let me know what you think, no rush. All the best, Layla

Hey Nora, I finally got around to looking at the schedule you sent and I have a few questions. One, are we still doing the Sunday morning shift at the front desk, because I thought we agreed to drop that. Two, the breakfast attendant on Monday is listed as me but I'm actually on the training course until noon, so I need somebody to cover. And three, I think there's a typo on the 13th, it says 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. but that's 8 hours and we only pay for 7 and a half. Anyway, no panic, I just want to get it sorted before the printouts go out. Thanks a ton, Damien

I'm going to paste a long message from my landlord and I want you to do three things with it. First, summarize what he's actually asking me to do in plain English. Second, flag anything that sounds like it might not be legal in this country, and I'm not looking for legal advice, I just want to know what to ask a lawyer. Third, write me a blank reply that asks for more time, because the original deadline is the end of the month and I can't realistically move out by then. Keep the reply to maybe 5 or 6 sentences, and please don't make me sound desperate. Just calm and firm. Okay, here's the message.

Here's what happened with the 10 situation. I went to pick up the rental this morning and the guy told me they only had the 4-person one left, not the 6-person like we booked. I said that's not what was on the confirmation, he said the system must've been wrong, and I went back and forth with him for 10 minutes. In the end he gave me the 4-person at no charge and a discount on the sleeping bags, which is fine, but it means two people are going to have to bring their own Tetra Sherard. I'd say Pedro and Sillin since they're the ones who said they have a spare. Can you two confirm?

Dear Mrs. Cassoana, I am sorry to hear about your experience during your stay with us last week. Having reviewed the records, I can see that you were moved from the garden suite to a standard double without prior notice, and that the air conditioning in the second room was not working for the first night. This is not the standard we aim for. I have arranged a refund of two nights, which is £380, and it should appear on your card within five working days. I would also like to offer you a complimentary dinner on your next visit. Please accept my sincere apologies. Yours sincerely, Diego Torres, Duty Manager

Hi Professor, I hope you're well. I wanted to give you a quick update on the thesis. I've finished the second chapter, which is the one on soil microbes, and I'm about halfway through the methods. The main thing holding me up is the incubation experiment, because the chamber broke on Monday and the replacement part won't arrive until the 21st. So I might have to push the third chapter back by about two weeks. I know that's not ideal given our deadline. I've talked to Layla and she says I can borrow her chamber for a few days, which should save me, but I need your approval to use the shared lab space. Thanks, Adrian

Okay, the story about the sinkhole is going live in 20 minutes and I just want to walk through the final checklist. The headline has been approved by the editor, the photo credit is fixed, and legal has signed off on the quote from the homeowner. What's still open is the map graphic, which I think Damien is finishing right now, and the push notification text, which I hadn't seen. I'd like it to say, quote, sinkhole closes road, and nothing more dramatic than that. Also, can somebody double-check that the link goes to the right section? Last time it went to the homepage and it was embarrassing. Thanks, everybody.

Hi Layla and the rest of the club, I've got some thoughts about next month's pick. I know a lot of us liked the idea of the big Russian novel, but I'm worried that at 900 pages it's going to kill the vibe. I'm not saying we should avoid hard books, I just think we should maybe, I don't know, split it over two months. The other option is the poetry collection, which is short and weirdly funny. Honestly, I'd be happy with either. I'll bring the wine either way. See you on the 4th, Nora

Hello Marco, thanks for your patience on the repair. Here's where things stand. The crew found that the leak was actually coming from the connection at the meter and not the main, which is why the first fix did not work. We've now replaced that fitting and the pressure on your street should be back to normal by this evening. You may notice some cloudy water for a few hours, that's just air in the pipes and it's harmless, but run the cold tap for a couple of minutes to clear it. If it's still cloudy tomorrow morning, please call the line. Reference number 44719. Thank you again.

Camping weekend packing list and who's responsible. Diego, you've got the tent, two sleeping mats, and the repair kit. Mora is handling the food, which is breakfast for six, burgers on Saturday night, and trail mix for the hike. I'll take the stove, the gas canisters, the pots, and the first aid kit. Somebody needs to remember the can opener this time, we got caught out last year with the beans. Also headlamps for everyone, a deck of cards, and a bag for rubbish. I think that's everything, but if you think of something, just add it to the shark.

Good evening everyone. I wanted to say a huge thank you to those who came to the reading on Thursday. We had 43 people in the room, which is almost double our usual turnout, and the author stayed for nearly an hour afterwards signing copies. A few practical notes. The sound system cut out for maybe 2 minutes during the Q&A, and I'll look into that before the next event. We also sold out of the paper box, so if you wanted one, I can take names for the reorder. Finally, the next meeting is on the 27th, because the library is closed on the 26th. Hope to see you there, She's a

I want you to act as an editor for a newspaper column. Here's the situation. I've written about 800 words on the plan to close the downtown parking garage, and the tone is too angry, I can hear it when I read it back. I don't want you to change my argument or cut any of the facts, just soften the language where I'm being personal about the mayor. Keep my paragraph structure the same, keep the British spelling, and don't add any quotes that I didn't write. When you're done, give me a list of every sentence you changed so I can check it out. Then one by one I'll paste the column in the next message.

Hi Nora, I wanted to follow up on the draft you sent for the weekend supplement. I read it twice and honestly it's close. The opening about the market stall is lovely, but the middle section drifts, you spend three paragraphs on the history of the square and I lost the thread of the story. Could you trim that to one paragraph and bring the vendor back in earlier? The quotes are good, but make sure you have the surname spelled right for the cheese cellar, I think it's with a double l. We need the final by next Wednesday at noon. Thanks, and nice work, Adrian

Dude, I finally talked to the guy at the hotel about the booking and it's a total mess. They have us down for the wrong dates, we're in from the 9th to the 12th instead of the 11th to the 14th, and the room we asked for is already taken. He was actually pretty nice about it though, he said he can put us in a bigger room for the same price if we don't mind being on the top floor. I said yeah probably but I have to check with you first. What do you think, are you cool with this terrorist? Let me know tonight because he needs an answer by tomorrow morning. Also, we should split the deposit.

Hi Pedro, thanks for the reservation confirmation for the lakeside site. A couple of questions before I pay the deposit. One, is the site pet-friendly, because we're bringing a dog, a very small and extremely well-behaved dog. Two, is there a water tap near the site or do we have to carry water from the main building? Three, what's the policy on campfires, since we've seen on the website that there's a fire ban in some areas. If there's a charge for the extra car, just let me know and I'll sort it. We're planning to arrive around 5 on Friday and leave Sunday at noon. Thanks very much. Cheer up

Quick update on the lab move. The freezers are going first, on Monday morning, and the movers will need us to label every box with the room number and the owner's name. I know that sounds basic but last time half of them just said fridge. The microscopes go on Tuesday and Wednesday and they have to be a sign of I had a technician before and after. We have until Friday to clear the benches, or they'll be sorted for us, which I really don't want. The new lab should be ready by the following Monday, though honestly I'd plan for it to be a day or two later. Shut if you need boxes, I've got about 50 spare.

Hi Diego, hope the trip back was okay. I just wanted to say that the retreat was really useful and I came back with a lot of ideas. The session on how to handle difficult guests was probably my favorite, the part about listening first and only offering a solution afterwards, which sounds obvious but isn't when you're tired. I'd like to try running a short version of it at our next staff meeting if that's all right. I can use about 50 minutes. Also, there's a spare ticket for the hospitality conference in March, if you or someone on the team wants it, it's free but you'd need to book your own travel. Cheers

Okay, update on the camping plans because I've been going back and forth. I know I said I'd bring the cooler but my car's making this weird noise and I'm kind of scared to take it on the highway. So could someone pick me up, or could I ride with you guys? I can chip in for gas obviously, and I'll bring all the snacks and drinks to make up for it. Also, I found this really cool spot about 20 minutes past the lake, apparently there's a hot spring, and I think we should check it, Bob, on Saturday. Anyway, let me know what works. If not, I'll just take the bus.

Dear Professor Ferrer, I hope this message finds you well. I am a second-year PhD student in the Department of Chemistry, and I am writing to ask if you would be willing to serve on my thesis committee. My work focuses on catalysts for hydrogen production, and I believe your expertise in electrochemistry would be valuable. The committee meets twice a year, in April and October, and each meeting lasts about 2 hours. I would of course send all materials at least two weeks in advance. I have attached a one-page summary of my research. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, Damien Roth
